desc:
Count the integers x with 0 ≤ x ≤ n whose binary representation contains an even number of 1 bits. Zero has no 1 bits, so it counts.

n = 0 -> 1   (only 0)
n = 3 -> 2   (0, and 3 = 11 in binary)
n = 7 -> 4   (0, 3, 5 = 101 and 6 = 110)
hints: Make a small table of 0 to 7 with the number of 1 bits of each. Do you see a pattern in the parity of the counts?
Go through the bits of n from the top. Each time n has a 1 at position i, you may place a 0 there instead and let the i lower bits take any value.
If i is at least 1, exactly half of the 2<sup>i</sup> choices for the lower bits give an even total. Handle the lowest bit on its own, and finish by checking n itself.
editorial: Walk down the bits of n from the top, keeping ones, the number of 1 bits in the prefix of n matched so far. A number below n is classified by the first position i where it differs from n. At that position n has a 1 and the number has a 0, the bits above i agree with n, and the i lower bits are free.

The free bits give 2i numbers. If i ≥ 1, the lower bits have an even popcount for exactly half of them, so exactly 2i-1 of them give an even total no matter what ones is. If i = 0 there is a single candidate, and it counts when ones is even.
Finally n itself counts if its popcount is even. The loop runs over the bits of n, so the whole count takes O(log n) time.
